hook.line: Hernando is dictating his memoir, and Tomás keeps asking what he thinks about one old decision. A view he has held ever since needs a different tense from the day it happened.
hook.es: Siempre he pensado que fue un error.
hook.en: I've always thought it was a mistake.

examples.es: Siempre he pensado que fue un error.
examples.en: I've always thought it was a mistake.

examples.es: Este año no he podido descansar.
examples.en: I haven't been able to rest this year.

examples.es: Nunca he entendido por qué renunció.
examples.en: I've never understood why she resigned.

examples.es: Siempre he creído que Rosa tenía razón.
examples.en: I've always believed that Rosa was right.

examples.es: Esta semana no he podido llamar a mi mamá.
examples.en: I haven't been able to call my mom this week.

examples.es: Hernando nunca ha aceptado la oferta.
examples.en: Hernando has never accepted the offer.

rule:
In Latin America, the simple past is the everyday tense for events that are over: *Ayer no pude descansar*.

The *he* + participle form is for what is still open: a view you still hold (*siempre he pensado*, *nunca he entendido*) or a stretch of time you are still in (*este año*, *esta semana*).

Look at the first example. *Siempre he pensado* is the view, still alive. *Que fue un error* is the closed event, so it stays in the simple past.

Don't use *he* for a finished yesterday.
smallPrint: Teachers call *he pensado* the present perfect. Here it marks something that began earlier and is still true now.

readAndPick.es: Siempre he pensado que fue un error.
options: I always thought it was a mistake, but not any more.
I've always thought it was a mistake.
I'll always think it's a mistake.
I haven't been able to rest this year.
I won't be able to rest tomorrow.
I couldn't rest yesterday.

readAndPick.es: Este año no he podido descansar.
options: I haven't been able to rest this year.
I couldn't rest last year.
I couldn't rest yesterday.

readAndPick.es: Nunca he entendido por qué renunció.
options: She has never understood why I resigned.
I never resign without understanding why.
I've never understood why she resigned.

readAndPick.es: Hernando nunca ha aceptado la oferta.
options: Hernando has never accepted the offer.
Hernando never accepted the offer that day.
I have never accepted the offer.

readAndPick.es: Esta semana no hemos vendido casi nada.
options: I haven't sold much this week.
We didn't sell much last week.
We haven't sold much this week.

readAndPick.es: El año pasado no pude viajar.
options: I haven't been able to travel this year.
I couldn't travel last year.
I couldn't travel this year.

readAndPick.es: Siempre he sentido que el café me esperaba.
options: The café has always waited for me.
I felt the café was waiting for me that day.
I've always felt that the café was waiting for me.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *pensé* or *he pensado*: Siempre ___ que fue un error. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Siempre he pensado que fue un error.
yourTurn.why: The view is still alive today, so it takes *he pensado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *no pude* or *no he podido*: Este año ___ descansar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Este año no he podido descansar.
yourTurn.why: This year isn't over yet, so the perfect fits.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *no pude* or *no he podido*: Ayer ___ descansar. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: Yesterday is closed, so the simple past.

yourTurn.prompt: I've never understood why she resigned.
yourTurn.answer: Nunca he entendido por qué renunció.
yourTurn.why: *Nunca he entendido* is the view that still stands; *renunció* is the closed event.

yourTurn.prompt: I haven't been able to call my mom this week.
yourTurn.answer: Esta semana no he podido llamar a mi mamá.
accept: No he podido llamar a mi mamá esta semana.
yourTurn.why: The week is still running, so *no he podido*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Hernando: *Nunca he aceptado la oferta.*
yourTurn.answer: Hernando nunca ha aceptado la oferta.
accept: Él nunca ha aceptado la oferta.
yourTurn.why: Only the helper changes: *he* becomes *ha* for *he* or *she*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: *Siempre he creído que Rosa tenía razón.*
yourTurn.answer: Siempre hemos creído que Rosa tenía razón.
accept: Nosotros siempre hemos creído que Rosa tenía razón.
yourTurn.why: *Hemos* is the *we* helper; *tenía* stays the same.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Yesterday is finished, and in Latin America a finished day takes the simple past.

pitfalls.wrong: Siempre he pensado que ha sido un error.
pitfalls.right: Siempre he pensado que fue un error.
pitfalls.why: Only the view is still alive. The mistake itself is a closed event, so it takes *fue*.

pitfalls.wrong: Nunca he entendido por qué ha renunciado.
pitfalls.right: Nunca he entendido por qué renunció.
pitfalls.why: The resignation happened once and is over, so keep it in the simple past.

personal: Tell me one thing you have always thought about a decision, yours or someone else's. Start with *Siempre he pensado que…* and put the decision itself in the simple past.
